user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Prerequisites (Night Before)

```bash
# Install required tools
git --version          # Git 2.x+
git svn --version      # git-svn bridge
svnadmin --version     # SVN admin tools (optional)
```

---

## Timeline Overview

| Time | Phase | Duration |
|------|-------|----------|
| 08:00 | Prep & Backup | 1 hr |
| 09:00 | Author Mapping | 30 min |
| 09:30 | Migration | 1 hr |
| 10:30 | Cleanup & Verification | 1 hr |
| 11:30 | Remote Setup | 30 min |
| 12:00 | Lunch Break | 1 hr |
| 13:00 | Team Switchover | 2 hr |
| 15:00 | Validation & Testing | 1 hr |
| 16:00 | Buffer / Rollback Window | 1 hr |
| 17:00 | Done ✅ | — |

---

## Phase 1 — Prep & Backup (08:00–09:00)

### 1.1 Lock the SVN Repo (Freeze Commits)
```bash
# Notify team — no commits during migration
svnadmin lock /path/to/svn/repo
# OR set repo to read-only via server config
```

### 1.2 Full SVN Backup
```bash
svnadmin dump /path/to/svn/repo > svn-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).dump
# Verify dump
wc -l svn-backup-*.dump
```

### 1.3 Gather Repo Info
```bash
# Check revision count
svn info http://svn.example.com/repo

# List all authors (you'll need these)
svn log http://svn.example.com/repo -q | \
  grep "^r" | \
  awk '{print $3}' | \
  sort -u > authors-raw.txt

cat authors-raw.txt
```

---

## Phase 2 — Author Mapping (09:00–09:30)

### 2.1 Create authors.txt
```
# Format: svn_username = Full Name <email>
jsmith = John Smith <jsmith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mjones@company.com>
deploy = CI Bot <ci@company.com>
```

```bash
# Verify no authors are missing
svn log http://svn.example.com/repo -q | \
  grep "^r" | awk '{print $3}' | sort -u | \
  while read user; do
    grep "^$user " authors.txt || echo "MISSING: $user"
  done
```

---

## Phase 3 — Migration (09:30–10:30)

### 3.1 Clone SVN → Git

**Standard layout (trunk/branches/tags):**
```bash
git svn clone http://svn.example.com/repo \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -A authors.txt \
  my-project-git

# --no-metadata    = cleaner commit messages (remove git-svn-id lines)
# --stdlayout      = maps trunk→main, branches/*, tags/*
```

**Non-standard layout:**
```bash
git svn clone http://svn.example.com/repo \
  --trunk=trunk \
  --branches=branches \
  --tags=releases \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  my-project-git
```

**Flat repo (no branches):**
```bash
git svn clone http://svn.example.com/repo \
  --authors-file=authors.txt \
  my-project-git
```

### 3.2 Monitor Progress
```bash
# In another terminal — watch commit count
cd my-project-git && git log --oneline | wc -l
```

---

## Phase 4 — Cleanup (10:30–11:30)

### 4.1 Convert SVN Tags → Git Tags
```bash
cd my-project-git

# List remote SVN tags
git branch -r | grep tags/

# Convert each to a proper Git tag
git branch -r | grep 'tags/' | sed 's/.*tags\///' | while read tag; do
  git tag "$tag" "refs/remotes/tags/$tag"
  git branch -r -d "tags/$tag"
done
```

### 4.2 Convert Remote Branches → Local Branches
```bash
git branch -r | grep -v 'tags/' | grep -v '@' | while read branch; do
  local_name=$(echo "$branch" | sed 's/.*\///')
  git branch "$local_name" "refs/remotes/$branch"
done
```

### 4.3 Rename trunk → main
```bash
git branch -m trunk main
```

### 4.4 Clean Up SVN Remotes
```bash
# Remove git-svn remote tracking refs
git branch -r | xargs -I{} git branch -rd {}

# Remove svn section from config
git config --remove-section svn-remote.svn 2>/dev/null
git config --remove-section svn 2>/dev/null
```

### 4.5 Add .gitignore
```bash
# Convert SVN ignores to .gitignore
git svn show-ignore > .gitignore
git add .gitignore
git commit -m "chore: add .gitignore from SVN ignores"
```

---

## Phase 5 — Remote Setup (11:30–12:00)

### 5.1 Create Remote Repo
```
GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket → New Repository
- Name: my-project
- Visibility: Private
- Do NOT initialize with README
```

### 5.2 Push Everything
```bash
cd my-project-git

git remote add origin git@github.com:org/my-project.git

# Push main branch
git push -u origin main

# Push all branches
git push origin --all

# Push all tags
git push origin --tags
```

### 5.3 Verify on Remote
```bash
# Check branch count
git branch -r | wc -l

# Check tag count
git tag | wc -l

# Check commit count matches
git log --oneline | wc -l
```

---

## Phase 6 — Team Switchover (13:00–15:00)

### 6.1 Checklist Per Developer
```bash
# Each dev runs:
cd ~
git clone git@github.com:org/my-project.git
cd my-project
git log --oneline -10    # Verify history looks right
```

### 6.2 Update CI/CD
```
□ Update pipeline repo URL
□ Update branch references (trunk → main)
□ Update webhook URLs
□ Test a pipeline run
□ Update any deploy scripts
```

### 6.3 Update Project References
```
□ README links
□ Issue tracker / Jira project settings
□ Wiki / documentation
□ Slack/Teams integrations
□ IDE project settings per developer
```

---

## Phase 7 — Validation (15:00–16:00)

### Verification Checklist
```bash
# ✅ Commit count matches SVN
svn log http://svn.example.com/repo -q | grep "^r" | wc -l
git log --oneline | wc -l

# ✅ All authors mapped correctly
git log --format="%an <%ae>" | sort -u

# ✅ Branches present
git branch -a

# ✅ Tags present
git tag

# ✅ Latest files match SVN working copy
# Compare a known file
svn cat http://svn.example.com/repo/trunk/src/main.py
git show main:src/main.py

# ✅ CI pipeline green
# ✅ At least one dev successfully cloned and built
```

---

## Rollback Plan

```
If anything goes wrong before 16:00:
  1. Re-open SVN repo (remove lock)
  2. Notify team to continue using SVN
  3. Archive the Git migration attempt
  4. Schedule retry with lessons learned

SVN backup is safe at: svn-backup-YYYYMMDD.dump
```

---

## Quick Reference Card (Share with Team)

```
Old SVN Command          →  New Git Equivalent
─────────────────────────────────────────────
svn checkout URL         →  git clone URL
svn update               →  git pull
svn commit -m "msg"      →  git add . && git commit -m "msg" && git push
svn status               →  git status
svn log                  →  git log
svn diff                 →  git diff
svn revert file          →  git checkout -- file
svn branch               →  git branch / git checkout -b
```

---

## Post-Migration (Next Day)

```
□ Archive/disable SVN repo (read-only, don't delete yet)
□ Keep SVN backup for 90 days
□ Send team "Git basics" cheat sheet
□ Set up branch protection rules on main
□ Configure required PR reviews
□ Schedule Git workflow training if needed
```

---

> **Key Risk:** The `git svn clone` step can be slow on large histories.
> For a *small repo* (<1000 commits) expect **5–20 minutes**.
> If it's taking hours, something is wrong — check network/SVN server load.

## Top 3 Migration Risks

---

### 🔴 Risk 1 — Someone Commits to SVN During Migration
**Impact:** Those commits are lost and never make it into Git.

**Mitigations:**
- Lock the SVN repo **before** `git svn clone` starts
- Send a team-wide freeze notice the day before
- If missed → re-run migration from the dump backup

---

### 🔴 Risk 2 — Incomplete Author Mapping
**Impact:** `git svn clone` **aborts mid-migration** on any unmapped username, wasting time and producing an incomplete repo.

**Mitigations:**
- Run the author audit script in Phase 2 **before** cloning
- Pay special attention to old/bot/service accounts that rarely committed
- If missed → add the entry to `authors.txt` and re-run

---

### 🔴 Risk 3 — CI/CD Still Pointing at SVN
**Impact:** Pipelines silently build stale code, or break entirely — potentially shipping the wrong version.

**Mitigations:**
- Update **all** pipeline configs before declaring migration done
- Run a full pipeline end-to-end in Phase 6 to confirm
- Don't delete/lock SVN until at least one clean CI run succeeds on Git

---

> **Honorable mention:** Binary files / SVN externals — Git handles these
> poorly and may require extra tooling (`git-lfs`, manual re-linking)
> if your repo uses them heavily.

## Migration Day Checklist

**Prep**
- [ ] Back up SVN repo (`svnadmin dump`)
- [ ] Lock SVN repo (freeze commits)
- [ ] Notify team of freeze

**Migration**
- [ ] Audit and complete `authors.txt`
- [ ] Run `git svn clone`
- [ ] Convert tags and branches
- [ ] Rename `trunk` → `main`
- [ ] Add `.gitignore`

**Push**
- [ ] Create remote repo (GitHub/GitLab)
- [ ] Push all branches and tags
- [ ] Verify commit count matches SVN

**Switchover**
- [ ] Each dev clones the new repo
- [ ] CI/CD updated and pipeline runs green
- [ ] All repo URL references updated

**Sign-off**
- [ ] Spot-check files match SVN source
- [ ] SVN set to read-only (not deleted)
- [ ] Team notified migration is complete

If anything goes wrong, **restore from the SVN dump backup:**

```bash
svnadmin load /path/to/restored/repo < svn-backup-YYYYMMDD.dump
```

Then remove the SVN lock so the team can resume work as normal, and treat the Git migration as a failed attempt to be rescheduled.

> This is why the dump backup and SVN lock are the **first two steps** of the day.

**`git-svn` must be installed.**

Without it the migration command (`git svn clone`) won't run at all.

```bash
# Check it's available
git svn --version

# Install if missing
apt install git-svn        # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install git-svn       # macOS
yum install git-svn        # RHEL/CentOS
```

> Everything else in the plan depends on this — verify it the **night before**, not on migration morning.

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
**Compare commit counts between SVN and Git.**

```bash
# SVN count
svn log http://svn.example.com/repo -q | grep "^r" | wc -l

# Git count
git log --oneline | wc -l
```

Two numbers, two seconds — if they match you have high confidence the migration is complete. If they don't, something was missed before you go any further.
**08:00 Backup → 09:00 Author map → 09:30 Clone → 10:30 Cleanup → 11:30 Push → 13:00 Switchover → 15:00 Validate → 16:00 Done ✅**

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
1. **`git svn`** — migrates SVN history, branches, and tags directly into a Git repo.
2. **`svnadmin`** — backs up and restores the SVN repo in case you need to roll back.

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text:
The **project or team lead** — they are accountable for confirming that:

- CI/CD is green
- All developers have successfully cloned the new repo
- No commits are missing

before SVN is set to read-only and Git becomes the single source of truth.

Send a **single clear message to the whole team the day before** with three things:

> "SVN is frozen at **08:00 tomorrow**. Do not commit after that time. You will be on Git by **end of day**."

Short, specific, and leaves no room for confusion.

## Final Recap

**Goal:** Move a small SVN repo to Git in one working day with zero history loss.

**Key steps in order:**
1. Back up SVN and freeze commits
2. Map all authors
3. Run `git svn clone`
4. Clean up branches and tags
5. Push to remote
6. Switch team over and update CI/CD
7. Validate and sign off

**Top 3 risks:** SVN commits during migration, incomplete author mapping, CI/CD still pointing at SVN.

**Rollback:** Restore from `svnadmin dump` backup and remove the lock.

**One prerequisite:** `git-svn` installed and verified the night before.

**Fastest validation:** Commit count matches between SVN and Git.

**Approval:** Team or project lead signs off before SVN goes read-only.

**Communication:** One clear freeze notice sent to the whole team the day before.

> If the checklist is followed in order and SVN is locked before cloning starts, this is a low-risk, straightforward migration for a small repo.

• Back up SVN first
• Lock repo, notify team
• Map all authors before cloning
• Run `git svn clone`
• Clean branches, tags, rename trunk → main
• Push to remote
• Update CI/CD, team clones new repo
• Validate commit counts match
• Lead approves cutover
• Set SVN to read-only, done ✅
